A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SciGenBench/ImgCoder study. The substantive text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: Tables 2–4 report original image-generation evaluations and downstream reasoning experiments. The appendices contain additional quantitative analyses and generated examples.

after.justification: The original benchmark and downstream results remain, and Section 5.3 adds a human preference study covering 500 samples.

M1.justification: ImgCoder retains the Understand–Plan–Code workflow, four planning components, model backbones and executable rendering. The identical Appendix E prompt and Appendix A implementation settings support interpreting the Section 3.3 rewrite as reframing, not a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same scientific sources, five subjects, 25 image types, SeePhys reference subset and downstream MathVision/Geometry3K coverage. The new human study evaluates existing scientific-generation outputs without introducing another domain or task scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 and the appendix comparisons retain their comparator memberships. The new human analysis rates six methods already compared in v1; it introduces no new baseline method.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 adds a supplementary protocol: ten STEM annotators compare outputs across 500 samples, with winner, both-good, both-bad and problematic-question options, followed by exclusion of problematic questions and Elo comparison. Existing generation and downstream settings remain unchanged; the addition does not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new human–judge consistency study directly tests the validity of the benchmark's automatic evaluators against human preferences, a substantive validation question not experimentally addressed in v1. The existing error taxonomy, distributional analyses, domain breakdowns, filtering comparisons and data-scaling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The human study introduces averaging Elo scores over 100 shuffled win–loss orderings and Pearson correlation analysis. These are repeated rating calculations, not additional model-training runs. No confidence intervals or comparable uncertainty estimates accompany the new results.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds human Elo estimates and correlations of 0.957 with inverse validation and 0.911 with LMM-as-Judge. Tables 2–4 and appendix results are unchanged, including the 77.87% Gemini-3-Pro-ImgCoder and 73.41% Nanobanana-Pro inverse validation rates. Figure 1 redisplays existing performance scores by release date.

T1.justification: The scientific-generation formulation and inverse-validation definition in Equations 1–2 remain unchanged. The added Elo and correlation analysis introduces evaluation procedures, without new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 3.3 narrow ImgCoder's presentation from a proposed logic-driven framework to an instantiated code-driven workflow and prompting baseline. The benchmark, precision–expressiveness trade-off and downstream utility claims remain. The introduction still retains the stronger framework wording.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly interprets the human correlations as support for automatic metrics as human-evaluation proxies and for Gemini-3-Flash's discriminative reliability. Section 3.3 removes the assertion of substantially improved compilation success. Existing failure-mode, domain-gap and scaling interpretations remain.

D1.justification: The new study specifies Elo initialization at 1500, scale parameter 400, update factor K=32 and randomized averaging, providing concrete reproduction details. Appendix A hardware, inference and training settings, Appendix E prompts and project-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the SciFlow-Bench citation in Section 2.1 and qualifies ImgCoder's positioning as an implementation of an existing code-driven workflow. The remaining related-work coverage and cited works are retained after accounting for reference renumbering.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the abstract and Section 3.3, with a new human-consistency subsection and corresponding cross-reference updates. Author order and date also change. The overall section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the release-date performance plot and the two-panel human-correlation figure. Existing figures and tables are retained, with float relocation, renumbering and surrounding text reflow; the established visual style and table structures remain.

improvement.justification: The 500-sample human study supplies useful validation of the automatic metrics that v1 lacked, while the revised abstract and Section 3.3 qualify ImgCoder's novelty more carefully. The gains are limited by absent uncertainty estimates and remaining ranking disagreement: Figure 5 places Seedream-4.0 above Qwen3-ImgCoder in human Elo but below it on both automatic metrics. Stronger novelty wording also persists elsewhere.
